headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure for large energy users, like data centers, back to those users, aiming to prevent these costs from being socialized across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Governor Signs Bills to Protect Ratepayers from Data Center Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation aimed at addressing high energy costs and ensuring data centers do not drive up costs for families. The bills protect Virginia ratepayers from shouldering the cost of new energy infrastructure investments by data centers and other high-load energy customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates local water authorities to report data centers' water consumption to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, transparency advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Be Made Public
news_summary: A new state law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, which will be available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide credible numbers and address concerns about the industry's significant water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulation
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for sound profiles and allowing localities to examine other environmental impacts before approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data centers, environmental groups, Del. Thomas.
news_headline: Sterling Resident Says Data Center's Generators Produced Excessive Noise
news_summary: A Sterling resident reported excessive noise and fumes from a data center's backup generators running for nearly 24 hours during a power failure, forcing him to leave his home. This incident highlights the ongoing community concerns about data center noise pollution, which HB 153 aims to address by requiring sound profile assessments for new facilities.
